_about: ONLINE HELP pages (PLAYER VS PLAYER > ONLINE > ONLINE HELP): title and paragraphs. 47123 is the port Pocket Wars uses (PORT in pw/net.py).

pages.title: PLAYING ONLINE
text: One of you HOSTS: pick a map and settings, and your game runs the battle (it keeps the board and rolls the dice). The other JOINS by typing the host's INVITE CODE.
The host plays GREEN, the guest plays TAN. The guest gets the map automatically, even one the host made in the map editor.
Only the host may need any setup. Joining just needs the code.

pages.title: THE HOST'S ROUTER
text: Home routers block connections coming in from the internet. When you host, Pocket Wars asks your router to open port 47123 by itself.
If the lobby says PORT OPENED, you're all set: send your friend the code.
If it says it COULDN'T OPEN THE PORT, open it by hand: see the next page. On the same Wi-Fi you never need to: the code works as it is.

pages.title: OPEN A PORT, STEP BY STEP
text: 1. Open your router's page in a web browser. It's usually 192.168.1.1 or 192.168.0.1. The address and password are often on a sticker on the router.
2. Find PORT FORWARDING. It may be under NAT, VIRTUAL SERVERS, GAMING or ADVANCED.
3. Add a rule: port 47123, protocol TCP, sent to this computer. The lobby shows this computer's address (THIS COMPUTER: ...).
4. Save, then host again. Your friend uses the new invite code.

pages.title: WINDOWS FIREWALL
text: The first time you host, Windows asks whether Pocket Wars (or Python) may use the network. Choose ALLOW.
Clicked no by mistake? Open WINDOWS SECURITY, then FIREWALL & NETWORK PROTECTION, then ALLOW AN APP THROUGH FIREWALL, and tick Pocket Wars (or Python).

pages.title: STILL CAN'T CONNECT?
text: Some internet providers share one address between many homes, and phone hotspots always do. Then no port can be opened, and the lobby says so.
Easy fixes: let your friend host instead, or both install a free VPN app such as TAILSCALE. With it on, the guest types the host's Tailscale address (like 100.101.102.103) instead of the code.
Also check that the host is still on the WAITING FOR YOUR FRIEND screen.

pages.title: JOINING
text: Type the code, or copy it from your chat and press CTRL+V. Letters that look alike (O and 0, I and 1) are treated the same.
You can also type an address instead of a code, like 192.168.1.5 on the same Wi-Fi.
If either of you quits, the other one's battle ends with CONNECTION LOST.
